title: Bandwidth Estimation
description: Estimate network bandwidth requirements to ensure users experience fast load times without bottlenecks.

data.text: **Bandwidth** measures how much data can flow through your network in a given time, usually expressed in gigabits per second (Gbps) or megabytes per second (MB/s). Estimating bandwidth prevents slow page loads and timeouts for users worldwide.
Bandwidth per second = Average page size × Peak QPS. Convert bytes to megabits by multiplying by 8, then to gigabits by dividing by 1,000.
Average page size = 50 + 200 + (12 × 500) + (15 × 20) = 6,450 KB ≈ 6.3 MB. At peak QPS of 17,361, bandwidth = 6.3 × 17,361 = 109,374 MB/s = 875 Gbps.

data.title: CDNs Reduce Origin Bandwidth
data.text: A Content Delivery Network caches static assets at edge locations. CDNs can reduce origin bandwidth by 60–80% because most requests never reach your servers.
With a CDN serving 80% of assets, origin bandwidth drops to about 175 Gbps. That is well within the capability of modern cloud providers, which offer 10–100 Gbps per instance.

Don't forget upload bandwidth. Users uploading videos, photos, or documents need symmetric or high-upload connections. A video platform might see 10 Mbps upload per active streamer. With 1,000 concurrent uploads, you need 10 Gbps of dedicated upload capacity.

terms.definition: The maximum rate of data transfer across a network path, measured in bps.

items.question: Should I use bits or bytes for bandwidth?
items.answer: Network equipment advertises in bits (Gbps). Application sizes are in bytes. Always convert consistently: 1 byte = 8 bits.

items.question: What happens if I underestimate bandwidth?
items.answer: Users experience slow load times, timeouts, and packet loss. Under pressure, traffic may be throttled, causing a poor experience during peak hours.
